title: opportunistic-kernel-hedging-and-survivor-set-allocation-for-paged-attention
creator: Nina Patel
description: Background: Our paged-attention runtime sees recurring decoder stalls when fragmented KV pages are repeatedly allocated then evicted across interleaved tenant workloads. Current allocation policies are purely LRU/size-based and kernel selection is static per-model variant. Goal: introduce an opportunistic kernel hedging strategy plus a survivor-set allocation layer that keeps small 'survivor' fragments pinned temporarily to improve decode continuity and enable kernel lanes to warm up without sacrificing overall residency fairness. This ticket covers design, prototype, simulation, and a staged rollout for runtime-1.23.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator demonstrates >=15% reduction in end-to-end 99th percentile prefill latency for mixed short/long prompts under the baseline traffic profile
No regression (<=2%) in average token throughput on our benchmark suite (bench/latency-2025) when survivor-set enabled
Feature gated and toggleable at shard-level; can be turned off without requiring model restarts
Integration tests exercising eviction edge-cases (fragment stitchback, stale survivor promotion) pass in CI
Clear observability: new console metrics for survivor_holds, kernel_hedge_switches and fragment_reuse_rate are emitted

notes: Design summary: 1) Survivor-set: small per-shard reservation (configurable bytes, default 2% of shard memory) used only for fragments with high recent reuse score. Fragments admitted to survivor-set get a soft hold counter that decays with time and access. 2) Kernel hedging: when a request matches a fragile decode pattern (short prefill followed by bursty decode), the scheduler may try a fast-low-memory kernel first and in parallel prepare a fallback full kernel in a separate op lane. If fast kernel stalls due to missing fragments, the fallback takes over. 3) Admission heuristic: composite score = alpha*last_access_count + beta*decode_contiguity + gamma*(fragment_compactness). Tunables allow ops to bias toward lower memory or lower latency. Tradeoffs: survivor-set reduces eviction churn but increases worst-case memory pressure if misconfigured; hedging increases temporary GPU utilization and requires careful backpressure to avoid amplification. Implementation decisions: use existing shard-level metadata to avoid global coordination; store survivor bitmap as compact bitset in shard header; hedging state kept per-request in scheduler with strict TTLs.
test_plan: Unit tests for survivor admit/release and scoring (automated)
Extend eviction-sim scenarios: interleaved tenants, short vs long-lived fragments
Microbench: instrument p99 prefill and decode stall counts for kernels A/B under hedging enabled/disabled
Chaos: forced OOM on a dedicated cluster to verify survivor eviction fallback and no crash
E2E: run canary on 5% of traffic with feature-flag; verify metrics for 48 hours
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag: runtime.survivor_set.enabled = false by default
Stage 1 (lab): run simulator + microbench, iterate on heuristics
Stage 2 (canary): enable on ~5% of hosts in staging-dedicated for 24h
Stage 3 (regional canary): enable on 10% of region A, monitor p99 prefill, kernel_hedge_switches
Stage 4: global ramp with automatic rollback if p99 increases >5% or memory pressure >3%
